subject: killer whale
title: Some Killer Whales Eat Dolphins. These Ones Hunt Beside Them

scenes.text: Some killer whales eat dolphins. These ones hunt beside them.
Off British Columbia, scientists stuck camera tags on salmon-eating killer whales.
In about two weeks, the cameras logged two hundred fifty-eight close encounters with Pacific white-sided dolphins.
The whales followed the dolphins down to sixty metres, into near darkness.
The likely reason: dolphin sonar finds big Chinook salmon. The whales catch them and tear them up. The dolphins grab the scraps.
And the dolphins get a bodyguard against the killer whales that do eat them.

description:
Camera tags on northern resident killer whales off British Columbia recorded 258 close encounters with Pacific white-sided dolphins in August 2020, with the whales following the dolphins on dives up to 60 metres.
Researchers think the whales may use dolphin echolocation to find large Chinook salmon, while dolphins eat leftover scraps and may gain protection from mammal-eating Bigg's killer whales.
Partnership or freeloading?
first_comment: The same waters hold Bigg's killer whales, which hunt marine mammals, dolphins included. Are the dolphins helpers, freeloaders, or just hiding?
